evidence.finding: Voice-platform monitoring reported intermittent call-processing delays across all queues at the 09:15 incident onset.
Mean service level fell from 88.9% before the incident to 29.2% during/after it.
Mean ASA increased from 26.3 seconds to 113.9 seconds during/after the incident.
All four queues experienced material degradation despite unchanged queue staffing, indicating a shared rather than localized mechanism.
Scheduled and logged-in staffing remained at 49; productive staffing and adherence slightly improved.
Offered volume was 7.6% below forecast at onset and averaged only 2.1% above forecast afterward.
Recalculated service level matched every reported interval exactly, with zero percentage-point variance.

primary_root_cause_detail: An all-queues voice-platform degradation causing intermittent call-processing delays began at 09:15, exactly when service performance deteriorated. Stable capacity, near-forecast demand, and valid metric calculations rule out the principal alternatives.
recommended_actions: Escalate the 09:15 all-queues voice-platform degradation to the platform provider and obtain component-level incident logs.
Validate call-processing latency, routing-engine response times, and media/session establishment across the affected period.
Apply platform failover or traffic-diversion procedures when processing-delay alerts recur.
Correlate recovery timestamps with ASA and service-level normalization, then document the incident timeline and preventive controls.

rejected_hypotheses.reason: Scheduled and logged-in headcount were unchanged, while productive staffing and adherence improved.
Center AHT declined slightly, and queue-level AHT changes were small and mixed.
Demand was below forecast at onset and near forecast on average afterward; low-growth queues also degraded severely.
No routing event was reported, and transfer rates remained stable or slightly lower.
Service-level recalculation matched all reported intervals exactly, and a contemporaneous platform event corroborated the operational impact.

stakeholder_summary: The service-level failure was most likely caused by an all-queues voice-platform processing incident beginning at 09:15. Staffing and AHT were stable, demand was near forecast, and the reported service-level metric was accurate. Moderate volume growth may have amplified the impact but was not the primary cause.
